fullLoadCurrentHeap.interpretation: Slightly lower observed current heap after steady scrolling in all four process medians on this VM; no forced GC, retained-live-object or representation-only attribution. Both sides show large before/after drops, so GC timing and ongoing instrumentation matter.

fullLoadWindowsSamples.interpretation: Lower medians of within-action observed maxima in all four process pairs. Only 1–2 external samples per action; values overlap. These are sampled whole-process working set/private memory, not exact peaks, retained Dart objects or a proven memory-saving amount.

partialOpen.interpretation: Current heap and end-of-phase RSS are lower at these partially loaded open checkpoints. Open durations differ, and collection/drain changes background progress. External 500 ms sampling covers 11/16 baseline but only 6/16 candidate actions; candidate process 0 has no in-window sample for any of its four opens. External open samples cannot support a balanced process comparison, and missing samples are never zero.

measurementBoundaries.heap: Current usage/capacity/external usage summed once per application isolate group, without forced GC. Before is before action setup; after follows the profile frame-delivery drain. Snapshot timestamps within that sampling call are not recorded.
measurementBoundaries.phaseRss: ProcessInfo.currentRss start/end plus an in-process 250 ms Timer sampled maximum. Event-loop delays can delay samples; this is not an exact peak. This timer differs from the separate 250 ms frame-delivery drain.
measurementBoundaries.csvWorkingSet: Windows Process.WorkingSet64 / 1MB from the external nominal 500 ms sampler. Includes the whole application process, native/runtime/profiling state.
measurementBoundaries.csvPrivate: Windows Process.PrivateMemorySize64 / 1MB, private committed process memory; not equivalent to resident working set or Dart heap.
measurementBoundaries.csvWindow: Exact root PID plus creation ticks and launchIndex, startMs <= epoch_ms < endMs. No halo/nearest sample or interpolation. Per-action observed maxima are summarized with equal action weights where available.

limitations: No allocation-throughput, retained-object, live-object-after-GC or exact process peak claim.
Heap differences and deltas include natural GC timing, prior action history and instrumentation; negative deltas are retained.
Long open is a partial-load state; steady_scroll follows verified full load of one million logical lines and no active content I/O.
Open actions shorter than the external sampler interval may have no in-window CSV sample; absence is not zero and coverage differs by side.
Repeated actions share process state. Four paired process medians describe one VM, not independent hardware replications.
All raw observations are retained. Do not pool runs or attribute the whole-PR comparison solely to representation.
conclusion: Report observed snapshot values and sparse sample coverage with units. Do not claim retained memory, allocation throughput, exact peak reduction, cross-machine generality or memory savings caused by ChunkedList.
